title: Strict reduction and inverse-image cone lifts are chain natural
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$, with its constant $\mathcal O_E$-action, on the small pro-etale site in its module universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For any flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], set $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_{P,n}(x)=x\otimes1$ and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Put $C(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$ with the actual coefficient-induced transitions $v_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), and $D(P)_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B(P)_n=\Gamma C(P)_n$. All towers are restricted to the single integral coefficient ring. For any strict tower $X$ with transitions $w_n$ put $s_X((x_n))=(w_nx_{n+1})$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For a strict tower map $f:X\to Y$ let $H(f)(b,a)=((\prod_nf_n)b,(\prod_nf_n)a)$. Let $c_X:\Gamma H(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(\Gamma X)$ be the normalized identity on both sectionwise product coordinates for a tower of $R$-module sheaves [def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison].

Put $\theta_{P,n}=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_{P,n})$ using the finite comparison $\kappa$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a), and define $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_{P,n})z)_n)$ and $\widetilde\theta_P(w)=(0,(\theta_{P,n}w)_n)$. Then $t_nr_{P,n+1}=r_{P,n}$ and $v_n\theta_{P,n+1}=\theta_{P,n}$, and both $a_P$ and $\widetilde\theta_P$ are chain maps. For every strict map $f:X\to Y$ of such sheaf towers, $H(f)$ is a chain map and $c_Y\Gamma H(f)=H(\Gamma f)c_X$.

For every chain map $h:P\to P'$ between flat-term K-flat complexes, let $h_D,h_C,h_B=\Gamma h_C$ be the induced maps of the displayed towers. The following strict equalities hold, including the zero shifted-product coordinates:
$$\Gamma(h_n)\Gamma(r_{P,n})=\Gamma(r_{P',n})\Gamma(h),\qquad h_{C,n}\theta_{P,n}=\theta_{P',n}g^{-1}h,$$
$$H(h_D)a_P=a_{P'}\Gamma(h),\qquad H(h_C)\widetilde\theta_P=\widetilde\theta_{P'}g^{-1}h.$$
In particular, for any family of strict tower maps $u(P):D(P)\to B(P)$ satisfying $h_Bu(P)=u(P')h_D$, the maps $e_P=H(u(P))a_P$ satisfy $H(h_B)e_P=e_{P'}\Gamma(h)$ as chain maps.

For the final conjunct, use functoriality of integralOperationsRoosMap and the assumed square v P ≫ map h = map h ≫ v P' together with the reduction-lift naturality equality from the component theorem; associativity gives the required transported-lift equality.

Steps 1-2: comparison (a) gives the chain map y->y(x)1 and (b) defines theta_m as g^{-1}(r_m) followed by it, with t_m theta_{m+1} = theta_m and the pi_m c_{O_E} linearity. I checked v_n kappa_{P_{n+1}} = kappa_{P_n} g^{-1}(t_n) on sections, using the uniqueness of sheafification (Stacks 03EK, sites-modules.tex l.3551; pullback 03D6 (2)). Step 3: with d(b,a) = (-db-(1-s)a, da), the n-th entry of (1-s)(Gamma r_n z) is 0, so a_P and theta-tilde are chain maps with zero shifted coordinate. Step 4: (1-s_Y)F = F(1-s_X) holds coordinatewise and H is functorial. The argument works for any towers with products, so it also covers step 8's use on the section-level towers D and B, although the statement phrases this clause for sheaf towers (advisory). Step 5: c_Y Gamma H(f) = H(Gamma f) c_X, checked through the roosFirst/roosSecond normalization and the joint-determination clause of def-trf-point-sections-roos-comparison. Steps 6-8: h_{C,n} theta_{P,n} = theta_{P',n} g^{-1}h follows from naturality of the sheafification unit, and H(h_B) e_P = e_{P'} Gamma(h) follows from H(h_B u) = H(u' h_D). Edge cases P=0, h=0, h=id, identity transitions, the n=1 boundary and single-degree complexes all hold. g = Spec(gamma) is an automorphism of s, as (b) requires, and R(s) = O_E. The proof uses only definitions, so no off-unit statement, no tool_uses, no cycle and no SGA. Duplicate search: lem-trf-strict-quotient-unit-condition states only the (1-s)-kills-units piece of step 3, which is elementary there; no node states this naturality.
